|url=https://californiabirthindex.org/birth/marcus_darell_williams_born_1985_17169268 |website=CaliforniaBirthIndex.org |accessdate=2024-06-21}} (born December 3, 1985) is an American former professional [[basketball]] player. He played with numerous teams across Europe and Asia. Standing at {{height|ft=6|in=3}}, he plays the [[point guard]] position. He was selected with the 22nd overall pick in the [[2006 NBA draft]] by the [[Brooklyn Nets|New Jersey Nets]]. Prior to becoming professional player, he played college basketball for the [[University of Connecticut]] (UConn). ==High school and college== Williams attended and played for [[Crenshaw High School]] in [[Los Angeles]], California for his 9th, 10th, and 11th years, and transferred to [[Oak Hill Academy (Virginia)|Oak Hill Academy]] (Mouth of Wilson, Virginia) for his 12th year (2002–2003). During his freshman year at [[UConn Huskies men's basketball|UConn]], Williams was suspended for part of the season because of poor grades. As a sophomore in the 2004–05 season, Williams averaged 9.6 points and 7.8 assists a game. He was named [[Big East Conference Men's Basketball Most Improved Player|Big East Conference Most Improved Player]]. In his junior year, he was kicked off the men's basketball team for several months, for attempting to sell stolen laptop computers along with teammate [[A. J. Price]].{{Cite web |url=http://nbcsports.msnbc.com/id/10589616/ |title=Laptop thief Williams rejoins UConn |access-date=2009-01-01 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090315151355/http://nbcsports.msnbc.com/id/10589616/ |archive-date=2009-03-15 |url-status=dead }} Williams averaged 12.3 points, 8.6 assists, and shot 86% from the free throw line. In a game against Notre Dame, he recorded the sixth [[Double (basketball)|triple-double]] in UConn history with 18 points, 13 assists, and 10 rebounds.[https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=260520041 UConn squanders 19-point lead as Irish rally to force OT] In the [[2006 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|2006 NCAA tourney]], he averaged 20 points, 8.8 assists, while shooting 52% from the field, 56% from three-point range, and 96% from the free throw line. Williams scored a career-high 26 points in a memorable 98–92 [[Overtime (sports)|overtime]] Sweet 16 win against Washington on March 24, 2006.[https://web.archive.org/web/20120926175723/http://scores.espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=264000022 After slow start, UConn outlasts UW in OT in classic dogfight] ==Professional career== ===NBA career=== ====New Jersey Nets (2006–2008)==== Williams was selected 22nd overall in the [[2006 NBA draft]] by the [[Brooklyn Nets|New Jersey Nets]], using the pick they got from the Denver Nuggets in a trade for [[Kenyon Martin]]. Former teammates [[Josh Boone (basketball)|Josh Boone]], [[Rudy Gay]], [[Hilton Armstrong]], and [[Denham Brown]] were also selected, with all but Brown being first-round picks. Marcus Williams was named to the Rookie team for the 2007 [[T-Mobile US|T-Mobile]] [[Rookie Challenge]] at the [[2007 NBA All-Star Game|2007 NBA All-Star Weekend]]. As a rookie in 2006–07, Williams played in 79 games, averaging 6.8 ppg and 3.3 apg. ====Golden State Warriors (2008–2009)==== On July 22, 2008, Marcus Williams was traded by the Nets to the [[Golden State Warriors]] for a conditional first-round pick.[http://www.nba.com/warriors/news/warriors_acquire_marcus_williams.html Warriors Acquire Guard Marcus Williams From New Jersey] On March 10, 2009, he was released by the team. ====Memphis Grizzlies (2009–2010)==== In July 2009, Williams began playing on the [[Memphis Grizzlies]] Summer League team in Las Vegas, Nevada. He joined [[2009 NBA draft|2009]] first-round pick [[Hasheem Thabeet]], undrafted rookie free agent [[Jeff Adrien]], and [[Rudy Gay]] as one of four former [[Connecticut Huskies men's basketball|UConn Huskies]] on the Grizzlies' Summer League roster. On August 7, 2009, Williams officially signed with the [[Memphis Grizzlies|Grizzlies]].{{cite web| url=http://www.nba.com/grizzlies/news/grizzlies_sign_point_guard_marcus_williams.html |title=Grizzlies sign point guard Marcus Williams |date=2009-08-07 |work=[[NBA.com]] |access-date=2009-08-07}} ===International career=== ====Piratas de Quebradillas (2009)==== [[File:Marcus Williams (1).jpg|thumbnail|right|Williams during his tenure with [[BC Enisey|Enisey Krasnoyarsk]] in 2010]] [[File:Estudiantes vs Unicaja Málaga - 03.jpg|thumbnail|right|Williams playing with [[Baloncesto Málaga|Unicaja Málaga]] against [[CB Estudiantes|Estudiantes]] in 2013]] Williams signed with [[Piratas de Quebradillas]] of the [[Baloncesto Superior Nacional|Puerto Rican Basketball League (BSN)]] in late March 2009. During the first half of the season, Williams averaged 15.0 points per game, 5.3 rebounds and 9.3 assists. He had registered one triple-double and was the league-leader in assists.{{Cite web|url=http://www.bsnpr.com/jugadores/jugador.asp?id=2586&e=|title = Baloncesto Superior Nacional | Jugador}} He was also selected to play in the league's All-Star game and won the game's MVP award, as well as winning the Skills Contest. He also finished the season earning All-BSN First Team honors with teammate [[Peter John Ramos]], and helping the Pirates to the best record in the league. Because he went to the [[Memphis Grizzlies]]' summer league team and left the Pirates, he missed the league finals, and the Pirates lost the championship. ====Enisey Krasnoyark (2010–2011)==== In August 2010, Williams signed a one-year contract with the Russian team [[BC Enisey|Enisey Krasnoyarsk]].[https://thehoopsmarket.blogspot.com/2010/08/enisey-krasnoyarsk-signs-marcus.html Enisey Krasnoyarsk signs Marcus Williams] Quickly becoming leader of his new team, Williams helped Enisey qualify to playoff for the first time in club's history. In quarterfinals Enisey lost series to Lokomotiv-Kuban (1:2). Williams was named "Player of the Month" in Russian PBL League in November and December. He was also selected All-Star 2nd team. Williams finished season with 14.8 points per game and as league's best in total assists (184) and assist per game (6.8). ====Jiangsu Dragons (2011–2012)==== In late November 2011, Williams signed a contract with the [[Jiangsu Dragons]] of China.[http://sports.sina.com.cn/cba/2011-12-04/03585854560.shtml 挑战八一江苏不想三连败 新外援豪言要用胜利庆生] In 25 games, he averaged 11.1 points, 3.2 rebounds, 3.8 assists and 1.2 steals in 25.8 minutes.{{cite web|title=Marcus Williams player profile|url=https://basketball.realgm.com/player/Marcus-D-Williams/Summary/77|access-date=April 28, 2018|work=RealGM.com}} ====Unicaja Málaga (2012–2013)==== In 2012, Williams signed a one-year contract with the Spanish team [[Baloncesto Málaga|Unicaja Málaga]]. In 53 games, he averaged 9.6 points, 2.6 rebounds and 3.3 assists in 22.2 minutes. ====Lokomotiv Kuban Krasnodar (2013–2014)==== On August 19, 2013, Williams signed a contract with the Russian team [[PBC Lokomotiv Kuban|Lokomotiv Kuban Krasnodar]].{{cite web|title=Lokomotiv Kuban announced Marcus Williams|url=http://www.sportando.net/eng/europe/russia/61769/lokomotiv-kuban-announced-marcus-williams.html|work=Sportando.net|access-date=19 August 2013}}{{cite web|title=Marcus Williams signed with "Loko"|url=http://en.lokobasket.com/news/1908033.html|work=lokobasket.com|access-date=19 August 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140117032156/http://en.lokobasket.com/news/1908033.html|archive-date=17 January 2014|url-status=dead}} In 47 games, he averaged 9 points, 2.6 rebounds and 4.2 assists in 25.6 minutes. ====Crvena zvezda (2014–2015)==== On August 15, 2014, Williams signed a one-year deal with Serbian team [[KK Crvena zvezda|Crvena zvezda]].{{cite news|title=Crvena Zvezda puts Williams at point|url=http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/140146/180|access-date=15 August 2014|work=Euroleague.net}} On November 22, 2014, in a game against [[Galatasaray S.K. (men's basketball)|Galatasaray]], Williams set a Euroleague record for the most assists in a single game (17).{{cite news|title=Crvena Zvezda's Williams breaks Euroleague assists record!|url=http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/145525/180|access-date=22 November 2014|work=euroleague.net}}{{cite news|title=Erceg, Arroyo star in Galatasaray's 2OT win over Crvena Zvezda|url=http://www.euroleague.net/main/results/showgame?gamecode=70&pcode=DHF&seasoncode=E2014#!report|access-date=21 November 2014|work=euroleague.net}}{{cite news|title=Vilijams ponovo sakriva loptu: Čudesne asistencije Zvezdinog pleja u Istanbulu (VIDEO)|url=http://www.mozzartsport.com/vesti/vilijams-ponovo-sakriva-loptu-cudesne-asistencije-zvezdinog-pleja-u-istanbulu-video/90102|access-date=21 November 2014|work=mozzartsport.com|language=sr}} He also added 8 points while shooting just 3–16 from the field. However, his team lost after double overtime with 110–103.{{cite news|title=EL: Erceg ukrao pobedu Zvezdi!|url=http://www.b92.net/sport/kosarka/vesti.php?yyyy=2014&mm=11&dd=21&nav_id=926813|access-date=21 November 2014|work=b92.net|language=sr}} With Crvena zvezda, he won the [[2014–15 ABA League|Adriatic League]] championship, the [[2014–15 Basketball League of Serbia|Serbian League]] championship and the [[Radivoj Korać Cup]]. On November 3, 2015, he re-signed with Crvena zvezda,{{cite news|title=Crvena Zvezda brings back point guard Williams|url=http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/6gbh9yhvnnej4apl|access-date=November 4, 2015|work=Euroleague.net|date=November 3, 2015}} but on December 28, 2015, he and the team parted ways.{{cite news|title=Rastanak Crvene zvezde i Vilijamsa|url=http://www.kkcrvenazvezda.rs/rastanak-crvene-zvezde-i-vilijamsa-28-12-2015.html|access-date=December 28, 2015|work=kkcrvenazvezda.rs|date=December 28, 2015|language=sr|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151230214220/http://www.kkcrvenazvezda.rs/rastanak-crvene-zvezde-i-vilijamsa-28-12-2015.html|archive-date=December 30, 2015|url-status=dead}} ====Budućnost Podgorica (2016–2017)==== On July 27, 2016, Williams signed with Montenegrin club [[KK Budućnost|Budućnost Podgorica]] for the 2016–17 season.{{cite news|title=Markus Vilijams pojačao Budućnost Voli|url=http://www.vijesti.me/sport/markus-vilijams-pojacao-buducnost-voli-897954|access-date=July 28, 2016|work=vijesti.me|date=July 27, 2016|language=sr|archive-date=December 22, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171222052118/http://www.vijesti.me/sport/markus-vilijams-pojacao-buducnost-voli-897954|url-status=dead}} On March 26, 2017, he was released by Budućnost.{{cite news|title=Budućnost otpustila Vilijamsa uoči revanša sa CZ|url=http://www.b92.net/sport/kosarka/vesti.php?yyyy=2017&mm=03&dd=26&nav_id=1244026|access-date=March 27, 2017|work=B92.net|date=March 26, 2017|language=sr}} In 27 league games, he averaged 10.3 points, 2.5 rebounds and 6.1 assists in 25.4 minutes, while averaging 12.3 points, 1.3 rebounds, 5.1 assists and 27. minutes in 7 Eurocup games. ====Cholet Basket (2017)==== On 29 March 2017, Williams signed with [[Cholet Basket]] for the rest of the season.{{cite news|title=Cholet signs Marcus Williams|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/france/230545/cholet-signs-marcus-williams.html|access-date=30 March 2017|work=Sportando.com|date=30 March 2017}} In 9 games, he averaged, 8.3 points, 2 rebounds and 3.4 assists in 23.1 minutes. ====Reno Bighorns (2017–2018)==== On September 26, 2017, Williams signed with the [[Sacramento Kings]].{{cite news|title=Kings Sign Marcus Williams|url=http://www.nba.com/kings/news/kings-sign-marcus-williams|access-date=September 26, 2017|work=NBA.com|date=September 26, 2017}} On October 10, 2017, he was waived by the Kings after appearing in two pre-season games.{{cite news|title=Kings Waive Marcus Williams|url=http://www.nba.com/kings/news/kings-waive-marcus-williams|access-date=October 10, 2017|work=NBA.com|date=October 10, 2017}} On October 21, he signed with the [[Stockton Kings|Reno Bighorns]], where he averaged 10.8 points, 2.9 rebounds, 6.5 assists and 26.6 minutes in 49 games. ====Second Stint with Piratas de Quebradillas (2018)==== On April 26, 2018, Williams was reported to have signed with Piratas de Quebradillas of the [[Baloncesto Superior Nacional]].{{cite web|title=Quebradillas tiene un nuevo armador importado|url=http://www.bsnpr.com/noticias/detalles.asp?r=+17064|language=es|date=April 26, 2018|website=bsnpr.com|publisher=Baloncesto Superior Nacional|access-date=April 27, 2018}}{{cite
